title: Count Word Frequencies
description: Given a list of words, return a dictionary containing the number of times each word appears.

examples.explanation: Each word is counted once for every occurrence.

hints: Use a dictionary whose keys are words.
Increase the stored count whenever a word appears.

title: Remove Vowels
description: Given a string s, return a new string with all English vowels removed. Treat uppercase and lowercase vowels the same.

examples.explanation: The vowels e and o are removed.

hints: Keep the characters that are not vowels.
Use a set containing a, e, i, o, and u in both cases.

title: Find Missing Number
description: Given a list containing n distinct integers chosen from the range 0 through n, return the one number from that range that is missing.

examples.explanation: The range is 0 through 3, and 2 is missing.

constraints: 0 <= len(nums) <= 1000, all values are distinct, 0 <= nums[i] <= len(nums)
hints: The complete range has len(nums) + 1 values.
Compare the expected range with the values that are present.

title: Rotate String Left
description: Given a string s and a non-negative integer k, return s rotated k positions to the left.

examples.explanation: The first two characters move to the end.

hints: A rotation larger than the string length can wrap around.
Use k % len(s) before slicing.

title: Intersection With Counts
description: Given two integer lists, return a list containing each value that appears in both lists as many times as it appears in both. The result may be returned in any order.

examples.explanation: 2 appears twice in both lists, while 1 does not appear in the second list.

hints: Count the values in one list.
When scanning the other list, use one copy of a value only when its count is still positive.

title: Longest Increasing Run
description: Given a list of integers, return the length of the longest contiguous run in which every value is strictly greater than the value immediately before it.
hints: Track the length of the current increasing run.
Reset the current length when the next value is not greater.

title: Evaluate Postfix Expression
description: Given a list of tokens representing a postfix expression, evaluate it using integer arithmetic. Tokens are integers or one of +, -, *, and /. Division truncates toward zero.
hints: Push numbers onto a stack.
For an operator, pop the right operand first, then the left operand.

title: Daily Temperature Wait
description: Given a list of daily temperatures, return a list where each position tells how many days must pass before a warmer temperature occurs. Use 0 if no warmer day exists.

examples.explanation: For example, 71 has to wait two days for 72.

hints: Keep indices whose warmer day has not been found yet.
When the current temperature is warmer than the temperature at the stack top, resolve that earlier index.

title: Kth Largest Number
description: Given a non-empty list of integers nums and an integer k, return the kth largest value, counting duplicate values as separate positions.

examples.explanation: The values in descending order are 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

hints: Sort the values in descending order.
The kth largest value is at index k - 1 after that sort.
reference_solution:
def solve(nums, k):
    return sorted(nums, reverse=True)[k - 1]

title: Shortest Word
description: Given a string containing words separated by spaces, return the length of the shortest non-empty word. Return 0 if there are no words.

examples.explanation: The shortest words are 'the' and 'word' has length 4, so the answer is 3.

hints: str.split() ignores extra spaces.
If there are no words, return 0; otherwise find the minimum length.
